text:
Mia Chen: Quick heads-up — I ran a profiling sweep on the refactor branch with activation checkpointing enabled across our 4xA100 TP/PP config. Seeing ~25% higher all-reduce time during backward, which is destroying our compute/comm overlap. perf-bot also tripped a regression alert.

Omar Vega: Can you paste the profiler output? which kernels are being chosen?

Mia Chen: Pasting the simplified breakdown I collected (per microbatch):
```
Baseline (no checkpoint): compute 110ms -> all-reduce 60ms -> idle 30ms
With checkpoint: compute 210ms -> all-reduce 140ms -> idle 90ms
```
Notice the all-reduce increases proportionally and idle jump — suggests we lost overlap because recompute shifts timing.

Lucas Park: Is this specific to our accumulation/batch packing heuristic? If recompute extends compute windows, it might move reductions into a window where other ranks are still computing.

Mia Chen: Exactly. Also saw kernel selection change for matmul on the recompute path — profiler shows we fall back to a different kernel (smaller GEMM) when sequence length + recompute pushes memory pressure.

Anya Singh: Which NV link topology? 4xA100 across 2 nodes or single node? That affects all-reduce shapes.

Mia Chen: Single node, SXM4, NVLink mesh. So inter-GPU bandwidth should be fine. This feels scheduling/timing rather than bandwidth cap.

Omar Vega: Could be our collective scheduling: we start async all-reduces when a layer completes, but recompute makes layer completion non-uniform. If one TP partition recomputes earlier, it posts AllReduce before others are ready, causing queueing.

Mia Chen: I captured a flame chart. Posting the hot slices:
```
rank0: forward | backward(layerN recompute) [compute long] -> all-reduce posted -> wait
rank1: forward | backward(layerN no-recompute) [short compute] -> all-reduce posted -> faster
```
The stagger creates head-of-line blocking in NCCL schedules.

perf-bot: AUTOMATED ALERT — throughput_regression: -18% on branch refactor/checkpoint-scheduling (compared to main). Profile id: pf_2026_03_15_0421.

Lucas Park: Two hypotheses: 1) recompute increases peak memory pressure -> triggers fallback kernels (slower) 2) recompute shifts timeline so all ranks' collective calls misalign and NCCL serializes them. Both could be true.

Anya Singh: How about trying micro-batch re-ordering or a lightweight barrier to re-synchronize before heavy collectives? Might recover overlap at cost of slight latency.

Mia Chen: Tried a tiny experiment inserting a sync on every N layers to realign, and all-reduce time returned to near-baseline but overall step time still up ~8% due to extra sync. Results:
```
with sync: compute 210ms -> all-reduce 70ms -> step extra 30ms
net regression: +8%
```
So sync helps but we pay for it.

Omar Vega: Could we change batching heuristics so we avoid hitting the fallback kernel on recompute path? e.g., adjust matmul tiling or reduce peak activation footprint (quantize activations for recompute?)

Anya Singh: Another angle: NCCL async progress tuning or using topology-aware all-reduce algorithms that are less sensitive to call ordering (tree vs ring). Have we tried switching algorithm at runtime depending on jitter?

Mia Chen: I swapped NCCL algorithm to tree for the layer groups and saw improved stability in timings (reduced variance), though mean all-reduce still slightly higher.

Lucas Park: Let's capture a few additional artifacts: tensor shapes at each collective, kernel selection logs (from CUTLASS/our kernel picker), and per-rank profiler traces. If we can correlate a kernel fallback event with a comm spike we can prove the memory-pressure hypothesis.

Mia Chen: Uploading artifacts to the perf bucket: s3://redwood-perf/pp-tp/recompute/1776503210/ — includes torch.prof, nvprof slices, kernel-picker.log, and a short script to reproduce.

perf-bot: NOTE — tests queued: 4xA100 deterministic run, 8xH100 exploratory run. ETA ~2h.

Omar Vega: Action items: 1) Lucas to add kernel-picker tag traces to profiler, 2) Anya to test NCCL algo and async progress flags, 3) Mia to run deterministic runs for both 4xA100 and 8xH100. Re-evaluate after runs.

Mia Chen: Sounds good. Also flagging this for the Optimize team — might be a good candidate for an automatic batching/kernelselection hint when checkpointing is enabled.

Anya Singh: Passing to optimize@ for visibility.

Mia Chen: Thanks all — will post updates once perf-bot finishes the queued tests.
